Title: Golden Tennets and Vote decks. Advice?

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
Our group has been playing with the SPTR (NL/GT Jyhad) for some time now,
and it is just great (All you CL people out there-Convert! Convert! We
played 4CL for a year and a half before switching to NL/GT, and we're
never goin back!), but as I just built a Stealth Vote deck (Nosferatu and
Malkavian), I have noticed that without the Vote pushing rules (which I am
perfectly happy to play without, mind you), vote decks without Presence
are at a great disadvantage due to the lack of any other vote card that
aproximates Bewitching Oration.

The Jyhad card set was designed with both vote pushing and NL in mind, so
as a result there was no reason to duplicate the effects of Bewitching
Oration with a redundant card. Surprise Influence is clearly a card
designed to allow vote defense in non voting decks, as there is no reason
to have it in a deck with either Presence or a vote deck where vote
pushing is alowed.

When vote pushing is removed from the equation, vote decks without
Presence suddenly have a great disadvantage when compared to vote decks
with Presence, as they need to have titles on the table, either by passing
Praxis Seizures or having Titled Vampires. The problem here is that
Titled Vampires are all big, and thus slow and expensive to get out (and
expensive to lose as your combat defense probably isn't that good, unless
you have Presence for Majest...oops, wait a minute.), and if you have no
titles on the table and no Bewitching Orations it is very difficult to
pass a Praxis Seizure with just the one vote on the vote card, as it is
likely that either someone will have either the Edge, a Primogen, or a
Political Action in their hands.

As an example, my current political deck is a Nos/Malk deck with Rake and
Volker thrown in (for obvious reasons) that has many small vamps (Normal,
Dimple, Duck) to call votes at stealth to avoid interception, and a few
Princes as vote back up. In a game I played last night, the Toreador
across the table got a lucky Info Superhighway and as a result got Anson
out before I got to call any Praxis Seizures (my deck is 10% Prexis
Seizures, mind you), and as a result, my deck was completely shut down
until I got out both Rake and Gilbert Dwane. Luckily, every other deck at
the table was a slow reactive intercept deck (by sheer chance), so my
inability to act for 4 or 5 turns did not cost me too much, but if my
Predator was, say, a S+B deck (which my defense against is voting Pool
gain and racing to kill my prey), I would have been ousted very quickly.

Because of the lack of vote pushing and a action modifier version of
Surprise Influence (which will never be printed as there is no need for it
in the actual rules), vote decks have the following options:

A) Have Presence. This negates a HUGE chunk of vote deck designs, mostly
the ones that can't be intercepted (and with no repeat actions, if all of
your votes are intercepted and you survive due to Majesty, you are still
shut down.)

B) Have Obfuscate and no Presence, and have to rely either on sheer luck
(winning a Praxis Seizure vote with ONE vote), or rely on slow, expensive,
and vulnerable Princes. Again, this negates a huge chunk of vote decks,
mostly ones that don't have to worry about it's little expendable vampires
getting killed, or are speedy enough to out race it's S+B preadator.

C) Use the Settites. This would be good, but the Settites are
non-Camarilla and thus can't be Princes (removing the Prince voting
angle), have fev Vamps with votes to begin with, and there are very few
smallish vamps with both Obfuscate and Presence (I can think of 1
four-Nepata, and then some sixes). This makes the Vote Settite deck slow
and unreliable.

If there were a action modifier version of Surprise Influence (and again,
there never will be), this would not be a problem, and if vote pushing
were allowed, this would also not be a problem (although it would re-open
a whole other set of problems, i.e. the 90 KRC weenie vote deck) [if you
are reading this and unfamilliar with the SPTR (NL/GT) rules, they don't
use the DC 6 card limit on restricted cards, but don't allow the
unrestricted throwing of Political Actions as votes. This is regarded by
many as the best way to play Jyhad, as the DC rules make very few people
happy. They alienate both the no limit camps and the card limit people].
What are ways to fix this that I am yet to think of?

would be possible to build the deck but it might not be any more
successful than it is now: if another vote deck with Presence was at the
table it would rule and even if there weren't any, all the other decks'
Surprise Influences and titles might be too much for the vote pusher
unless he was a weenie-vote-pusher.

would make the "I'm So Cool" card with one modification however. It
wouldn't be replaced until after the current action. That would bring it

C) 4 Four (or whatever) card limit Jyhad: A common attempt to fix what
are percieved as problems in the game with a blanket card limit. This
enviornment, while avoiding many foibles of the above enviornments, is
basically cutting off a hand to cure a hangnail. Under CL, most decks
that are not Stealth and Bleed decks are at a great disadvantage due to
the lack of redundancy in certain Disciplines. Obfuscate and Dominate
have tons of redundancy because most of those cards are Action Modifiers,
and thus need redundancy, while combat decks are screwed by the lack of
redundant Bums Rush cards, and Animalism intercept decks are screwed by
the lack of reduntant Animalism intercept cards, ect. A while ago, during
one of the periodic NL/CL debates, there were countless attempts to post a
satisfactory "Brujah Pitch" deck (basically a perfectly reasonable Brujah
deck that uses all long range Potence combat and Celerity to Blur Sewer
Lids and Thrown Gates) under a 4CL, and it constantly failed, as you could
only have 4 Sewer Lids, 4 Gates, and 4 Cars, which does not a Pitch deck
make. No one (who was not a 4CL advocate) ever responded to this by
saying "Well, how is it a bad thing that you can't make this deck?" (that
was not meant in any way as an attack at Doug, just making a point :-).
The general response was "Well, under NL rules, you can make any deck, and
have it work.", and thus was developed...

D) No limit Golden Tenents Jyhad (or the Sensible Persons Tourney Rules),
a common rule set that fixes all of the above foibles by disallowing vote
pushing (only one vote from Political Actions per vote) and repeat actions
(a single vamp can only try to bleed once per turn, regadless of
subsiquent untaps). This is regarded by many (including myself) as the
best way to play. It eliminates all degenerate combos (and The Corrupter
has a undefeated long standing challange to come up with a degenerate deck
in this enviornment), and allows almost all decks to compete on equal
standing. Which brings me to my point about Presence and votes.

Messages.Author: PDB6
Messages.Body:
(Part 3 of my monsterous post. Thanks for sticking around this long :-)

Because of a complete anomaly, decks that want to vote without Presence
are screwed, because the card set is designed under envornment A, and as a
result, there are no need for non Discipline cards providing votes for
vote decks. With vote pushing, all vote decks have a good supply of fluid
votes, and Presence just gives an additional edge. Because of this, there
was no need to make a non Reaction version of Surprise Influence, as it
would be deemed as "useless and redundant" under enviornement A, and no
one would use it (much like Concealed Weapon). Surprise influence exists
as a card to provide vote defense for non voting decks. An Action Mod
version of Surprise Influence, while incredibly obvious, is not absent
because it would be too powerful or broken, It does not exist because it
is not needed as the game is designed. Because of this, a huge chunk of
decks (vote decks without Presence) which were perfectly viable under all
of the above enviornments, are greatly disadvantaged under NL/GT, and
there is no good reason for it.

It is good and all to compare Presence and vote decks to Stealth and Bleed
as an example of how some clans are good at it and some aren't, but this
is not an intententional result of NL/GT, and is only the case due to the
lack of a very obvious card (Action Mod Surprise Influence). If Stealth
Vote, Gangrel Vote, or basically any non Presence based vote deck were
unduly powerful under non NL/GT rules and needed to be hamstrung, and this
was intentional, then that would be just fine. My point is that this
deficiency is unintentional, and as a result these decks are just as
screwed under NL/GT as "Brujah Pitch" (or any combat deck) is under 4CL,
and any number of perfectly reasonable decks are under DC rules, and not
for any good reason.

Again, the inclusion of a perfectly reasonable and obvious card would fix
this completely, but the card in question (Action Mod Surprise Influence)
will never be produced. If I could convince my group that Surprise
Influence should be able to be played as either a Action Mod or a
Reaction, or we invented our own card to use ("Boy I'm cool": Only usable
during a political action. Gain 2 votes. Non Discipline Action Mod."),
that would fix all of this, but that probably won't happen, barring
overwhelming local and/or net support, due to the "Aww, quit whining,
you're just pissed cause YOUR deck is screwed..." aspect of this sort of
problem. Oh, well. What to do.

(That's the end.)

Messages.Body:
Yeah, I guess that you are right about not being able to make a good vote
deck without Presence in NL/GT, but that seems to me to be somewhat
opposed to the intent of NL/GT Jyhad as I see it is, namely the ability to
make any deck you want and have them be balanced (excepting the well known
degenerates).

As the various play enviornments go, they all seem to put various limits
on worthwhile deck designs, and while NL/GT seems to have the fewest
limits, as I have pointed out, it effectively neuters a huge chunk of deck
designs (i.e. vote decks without Presence), primarily by accident more
than design. Take the following common play enviornments:

A) No card limits, no other restrictions (how the game was envisioned):
You can make any deck to do anyhting at all, and while most decks are
balanced and no deck designs are more powerful than any others, there are
a few degenerate designs that came up that the designers had never even
concieved of, like the Weenie Vote deck (crypt of all Catiff, lybrary of
90 KRC) and the Freaky Bleed deck (Using Freak Drive to untap and
Bleed/S:CE/5th Tradition infintely). Barring some exeptions, combat decks
are just as good as bleed decks which are just as good as vote decks. In
this enviornment, a non Presence stealth vote deck is just as compettitve
as any other design (except maybe the "all Gird Minions" deck :-), and
baring intenional degeneration and the use of acceptable numbers of cards
(i.e. 10 KRC, 10 Praxis, 10 Con Boon, a bunch of Masters, some combat, a
bunch of stealth+whatever), is perfectly ballanced and non degenerate.

B) DC sanctioned tourney rules (what the designers have decided is the
best way to fix things): The 6 card restricted list attempts to fix the
above problems by limiting the "broken" cards to 6 of each. While it is
somewhat sucsessful in fixing things like Weenie Vote and Freaky Bleed, it
hamstrings some perfectly legitimate decks (like a deck that relies on its
10 Majsties for combat defense, or a perfectly reasonable vote deck that
wants to use 9 Conservative Agitations). It has also been noted that it
is still perfectly possible to build a nigh degenerate Weenie Vote deck in
this enviornment that is still almost as effective as it used to be,
negating the main fix that this enviornment attempts to impliment. In
this envornment, again baring a few close to degenerate decks, you can
make almost any deck, as long as you don't want more than 6 of any
restricted card, and again, a non Presence Stealth/Vote deck is perfectly
playable and is just as good and balanced as all other deck designs
(assuming the builder is attempting to avoid degeneracy).

True, with vote pushing, a vote deck with Presence will generally beat out
a vote deck without Presence (much like a plain Potence combat deck does
just fine until it runs into a Potence/Celerity deck). On the other hand,
a vote deck without presence at a table without other main line vote decks
will do just fine in a vote pushing enviornment, but in NL/GT, a vote deck
without Presence is very hard pressed to get its foot on the first rung of
the ladder, as it is almost impossible to pass a Praxis Seizure on a
smallish (i.e. first turn) vampire with only the one vote from th
Political Action card, as at a table with 5 other players it is highly
likely that someone will have either the Edge or a single vote in their
hand. Thus, the deck needs to wait to get out a Prince or two, and
expensive and slow process compared to other strategies (any type of
combat can start killing imediately, and any type of bleed deck can start
bleeding with its first vampire).

My point about the hypothetical Action Mod version of Surprise Influence
is that while it would be a perfectly acceptable card, and would happen to
fix this entire problem in the NL/GT arena, it will never ever be printed,
because the in the standard Jyhad/VTES rules there is absolutely no need
for it. With vote pushing (the actual rules), this sort of card is
completely unneeded and redundant. It would only be needed (and produced)
if the Jyhad rules officially switched to "No vote pushing", at which
point the card would be produced imediately.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
WHONK!

I think you've hit the nail on the head here, Peter. Regardless of the
rules used, it's hard to see a reason why not to have a discipliness
action modifier to gain 2 votes. Perhaps you would say it could not be
used in conjunction with Bewitching Oration, but that's a side issue.

In my usual fashion, I've tried to build a vote deck without Presence.
Here are the tricks I've found:

1) The edge is one vote, if you can filch it (Night Moves, or a 1 pt
Gangrel bleed).

2) In monoclan decks, Justicars usually pass (unlike Praxis Seizures).

3) Telepathic Vote Counting (TVC) at superior (cancel a vampire's vote) is
effectively 2 more votes in almost any situation.

4) Theoretically, rushing hostile voters can help. I haven't yet made
this work, though.

5) Bribes (the card) helps. Buying votes by calling things for other
players can help too.

That said, all these tricks are basically inadequate. I have one
vote/bleed deck that only grazes on Presence - my auspex-centered
Visionaries deck - but it's only mediocre, and its success is critically
dependent on table position.

If you're playing with the Mask allowing unlimited uses of a specific
action modifier, I think you could get somewhere with a semi-degenerate
deck built around Masks and TVC. But that is, well, kind of icky.

I'm aware of your fondness for Nosferatu; and certainly, in this case, a
Nosferatu blackmail-and-trickery political deck is outrageously
appropriate. In addition to the disciplineless gain votes card, there
should be an action card Blackmail to "(D) Place this card on a vampire.
You may burn this card during a vote to force that vampire to cast its
votes either for or against the measure. This can result in the vampire
changing its votes." This might be a Nossie-specific card, or be
disciplineless.

But I digress. A disciplineless action modifier to gain votes is one of
those lacunae that cries out to be filled.

IMO, of course.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
pd...@aol.com (PDB6) writes:

>L. Scott,

>Yes, that the Action Modifier version of Surprise Influence will never
>exist due to the structure of the actual rules has been part of my point
>all along (I guess you missed it in my missaligned and segmented massive
>post :-)

I gathered, from the post that I replied to, that you were of the
opinion that ActionMod-SurpriseInfluence (AM-SI) didn't exist because
the rules structure supported Vote pushing.

My post (no longer quoted) was attempting to clarify that "This is not
the case (IMHO)."

It (vote push) did not exist even back when the rules were first written,
when 1-PA-per-action was painfully (sloppily) part of the rules.

But, you are correct in the opinion that, given the current official
ruling (and explicit counter-wording in the VtES rulebook), there is
no need for an AM-SI. Any clan (or random mix of vampires) can vote
effectively by stacking a library full of vote cards.

Whether that is a good thing or not is apparently a matter of taste.

There are no "generic" stealth gainers for the same reason. Self
votes and stealth are used for offense, and offense requires a
coherent strategy.

There are, by contrast, generic reply-votes (1 for a PA, 2 for Surprise),
as well as generic intercept (KRCG, Sport Bike, Winthrop, Atonement
(special restriction on youth of vampire, but close enough), etc.)

Someone, somewhere (Richard Garfield, probably), did this intentionally.

Adding vote pushing disrupts this balance. Why stock any Surprise
Influences when you can achieve a much more adaptable ploy with
Political Action cards?

PA - doesn't require an untapped vampire (or even a vampire at all)
to burn for a vote. And, if no one is voting to begin with, you
can convert your PA to an action. Any deck can use a Disputed
Territory, or KRC. And it can be used during a bloodhunt, to boot.
And, last and least, it can be used to boost a vote that you call
to burn a card in play (Like Archon, Arboretum, Gehenna, Legendary
Vampire, Archon Revolt, etc.)

Surprise - requires an untapped vampire (who can only play one). Can't
be used to call a vote. Can't be used during a blood hunt. Can't be
used during a vote you call.

The only benefit SI has is that it gives two votes instead of one.
The benefits of including 2 PAs far outperform this.

>Given that it does not and will not ever exist, non Presence vote decks
>are at a vast disadvantage under NL/GT, that they were not under in any
>other play enviornment. Yes, vote decks with Presence have always beat
>out vote decks without Presence, but without vote pushing, non Presence

An alternative rule to the "no vote push" half of the Golden Tenets was
originally suggested by Curt Adams: no deck can consist of more than 40%
(or 50% perhaps) vote cards. This rule is designed to eliminate exactly
the problem decks (Weenie Vote Push) and leave others unaffected. The
rule works because WVPs jam badly after the first few votes if non-votes
are 50-60% of their library.

I personally have never seen a non-weenie, non-theme vote deck that had
anywhere near 40% vote cards. The Corrupter has had decks with 35% vote
cards and felt that 40% could be a constraint on a real vote deck. My
feeling is that if it is a constraint, it isn't a major one.

The Corrupter and I had a long thread that discussed the pros and cons of
percentage restriction vs. no vote push. I never responded to his last
article in the thread because he asserted that a 50% WVP with Misdirection
/ Computer Hacking / Anarch Revolt would still be degenerate and it took
me a while to test the assertion. I did eventually test it and it turned
out not to be true. The 50% WVP earned about 10% more VPs than an average
deck. It actually did best when a vote deck was one of it's direct
opponents (prey/predator), because real vote decks are slow starters and
have no quick defense to WVP _or_ Misdirection bleed.

The principal advantage of No Vote Push is that you can't throw "useless"
vote cards on lopsided agendas and thereby easily dispose of them. I
personally don't feel this is of major concern, but to some people this
is quite important.

As I see it, the Percentage Restriction has two advantages: it changes the
rules least while still addressing the problem, and (since it is a deck
composition rule) it has the best chance of actually being adopted by the
Duelist Convocation for tournament decks.

>I agree, it should be harder to 'force' votes through without the
>appropriate skills, but the main reason for this Golden Tenet is too
>increase fairness. Not allowing any push (the calling Meth. gets 1 vote
>from the PA) makes card cycling _much_ more difficult, and places it in
>line with other strategies.

I think the difference between one tossed and no votes tossed
is not that great. Curt Adams, in an excellent article, classifies
Jyhad cards into three classes: ephemerals, transients, and permanents.
Permanents are the most difficult to cycle, transients less
so, and ephemerals easiest.

The current VTES/DC rules allowing unlimited vote push turn
vote cards into ephemerals. They flow through your hand
like water (or combat cards). We all agree, this is broken.

With a one-vote-toss (in addition to the card being used to
call the vote), votes are merely transients. In effect,
a vote card is a three-class card: it's an action, a
limited reaction, or an action modifier. In all three cases,
it's a transient, not an ephemeral. At most, you'll be
able to cycle only two per (unblocked) action. This hardly
compares to the ability of a combat deck to cycle cards.

Under the GT rules, vote cards are still transients, but only
actions and reactions. They're slightly less flexible -
you can only cycle one per action.

There are quite a few cards which have more than one class to
give them added flexibility. I have yet to see complaints about
the multiple classes of those cards on the newsgroup.

If you allow vote cards to be action modifiers in addition to
being an action or reaction, how does it break the game? They
are still transients, and only slightly easier to cycle. Is
there a qualitative difference?

I'd also note that the thing starting this discussion was
Peter calling for an action modifier version of Surprise
Influence. (Which Bribes is, IMO).

>In addition, if all titles on a table of 5 players equal out (so that all
>other players titles are equal to your own amount of titles) the opposing 4
>Methuselahs will typically have ~1.4 votes, on average. Two votes can be
>gained from the Edge and the Political Action if the vote is to pass (this
>requires more versatility, a good thing). With one vote push, the two votes
>can be gained by throwing down the extra political action.

To turn this on its head, since your opponents will usually
have 1.4 votes, you *must* have the Edge to give your vampires
a decent chance of passing a vote. Do we want to make either
presence or sneak a necessity for vote decks?

>Alan Kwan's original article on this mentions how fundamental the
>difference between one push and one political action are. I hope the
>above example makes it clear: that one extra push is too much (dropping
>the necessity of broad deck design and increasing card cycling in unfair
>ways).

I don't find the argument compelling, so far. I agree that unlimited push
allows unfair card cycling. I don't agree that precluding a
focussed deck design (the opposite of a broad deck design) is a
good idea. (And after all, these vote decks *still* have to
have ways to deal with combat and bleed.)

anyone who hasn't read them, both Curt Adams' articles and

Telepathic Vote Counting, Kindred Coercion, or Rush (or anything else,

I agree that it's close to impossible to make an overpowering vote deck
without presence. I disagree that vote decks with presence can just push
everything through at will. If this is happening then it's opponents
aren't putting in enough vote defence. In games with a small number of
players (less than 5 or 6 say) it's easier to stop them with intercept,
but in big games (the way Jyhad was meant to be played in my opinion) it's
very hard to just ram votes down peoples throats. If you see somebody
bring out a prince and then start calling votes, it's a pretty safe bet
that they're playing a vote deck so unless you've got intercept or a Bum's
Rush, you better bring out a titled vamp. If everyone else brings out a
titled vampire you will probably get an average of at least two more votes
per person and that should make the presence vote guy start to sweat. It
probably won't shut him down completely unless people start bringing out
IC's, but it will force him to either make deals with people to pass his
votes or call votes that at least one or two others will vote for.

Obviously presence gives vote decks an advantage, but that's mostly what
presence is for so that's as it should be. It doesn't give vote decks any
more of an advantage than the other skills do for what they specialize in.

- WVP Library under 50% Vote Limits:
- Crypt: Uma Hatch 3, 2 Igo the Hungry, 2 Delilah Easton, 2 Gideon Fontaine,
- Roland Loussarian, 2 Antoinette DuChamp, 1 of each of the remaining 7
- Caitiff

- Revolt; 5% Misdirection; 10% Praxis Seizures (no duplicates if possible);
- 35% KRC; 5% Dramatic Upheaval and 1st Tradition; 5% Bewitching Oration;

with a vote deck as the direct prey or predator of the WVP, the WVP scored
a total of 6 VPs (4 would be average) or 50% higher than normal. In the
other 4 games, the WVP scored 4 VPs: exactly average. Combining the two,
the win rate is 25% higher than average. Considering that in one game
where the WVP got 3VPs, it just barely avoided being ousted with 0 VPs,

Intercept. Especially WVP, where every intercepted weenie is a dead
weenie.

50% votes in its initial deal and could push more than one vote early.

called degenerate.

I don't know if there's much point in continuing discussion. I don't feel
that SVP is bad, but I suggest that Percentage Restriction is a viable
alternative for some play groups It accomplishes some of the same objectives
(eliminating WVP degeneracy). SVP has the advantage that vote cycling is
minimized. For certain play groups (those that never see non-WVP 40% vote
decks) PR has the advantage of effectively not changing the rules at all.
PR also has a better chance of being adopted by the Duelist's Convocation,
since it is a deck composition restriction rather than a rule change.

However, under PR you won't have that many "useless" vote cards in hand
to throw. Cycling _does_ go on in other decks to a lesser extent, but has
the important advantage that the cycled card is replaced _immediately_.
You can Undead Strength strike someone who has dodged in the hope of pulling
that Blur and really giving him/her a world of hurt. You can Mighty Grapple
against that Majesty in the hope of pulling that Psyche that will let you
pummel the weasel. You can Skin of Rock when you have a perfectly serviceable
Flak Jacket, looking for the Pulled Fangs that will really teach your enemy
a lesson. The immediately replacement is really a fairly important advantage
for the other strategies that cycle at a lesser rate than vote decks do.

Hoping for a shorter thread this time. :-)

Camarilla.

[PR == Percentage Restriction of the number of vote cards in a deck]

> > I might put in 4 Lextalionis and thereby have a decent chance of having

>

> As could be done with Golden Tenets and SVP.

You can't have it both ways. Are you saying that a SVP deck would be just
as likely to put in 4 Lextalionis as a PR deck? The library is a fixed
resource. Under PR, situational votes that would be dead weight under
SVP can instead be used to assist other votes. Under SVP, those situational
votes can only be discarded, and take library space away from cards needed
to pass votes (Bewitching Oration, etc.) or other necessary parts of the
strategy.

You assert that under SVP, vote decks have to work hard to get their votes
passed. I don't disagree with that assertion. When I state that under
PR, you have more flexibility to include situational vote cards in your
deck, I don't see how you can disagree with that -- it seems obvious.

> votes can only be discarded, and take library space away from cards needed

Your keying in on situational cards strikes me as interesting. My basic
point would be, if vote decks should have the leeway to put in
situational cards without, _real_ _cost_ in hand (they can be tossed on a
vote), why can't other decks have the limitations on situational cards
removed?

When cards hold space in a deck, if that space they hold is meaningless
(as is the case with WwEF and virtually the case with pushable votes in a
vote deck), you have achieved a bad environment.
Cards can be freely put in without cost to the deck on the
hope that they will prove useful, but with the knowledge that if they
don't they can be tossed and replaced immediately with a useful card (or
at least a card that can be tossed for a useful card). Vote pushing
allows vote decks _alone_ to do this. If vote decks can do this, why not
allow everyone to be able to put in cards that do, things that work like
Malkavian Dementia, or Brujah Frenzy, but with one exception, they can be
tossed if useless with costless ease (i.e., not loosing a discard phase).

This environment leads down (one of) Magic's failing point(s): decks
often beat each other not on their own merit, but because they have
"screw" cards thst trump their opponent.

Currently, if someone puts in Malkavian Dementias, the cost in a typical
game of having a MD in hand is a Master Phase or a Discard Phase (both
limited resources). The card might be useful, but might not, and is
usually included in those decks that feel they are deficient in defending
against Malkavians. To put it in for any other reason is to waste card
space in the deck. In GT (SVP), vote decks have the same restriction with
Conditional cards that the Malkavian Dementia has, it uses up a limited
resource: vampire actions.

Your suggestion is tantamount to saying that clan screw cards should be
able to be put into everyone's deck at no cost, tossable during the
Master Phase if useless for no cost, and tossable at other times for no
cost. The only difference is that you limit this ability to vote decks.

> You assert that under SVP, vote decks have to work hard to get their votes
> passed. I don't disagree with that assertion. When I state that under
> PR, you have more flexibility to include situational vote cards in your
> deck, I don't see how you can disagree with that -- it seems obvious.

Your right. It is obvious (as I said, I misunderstood your earlier
assertion), but it is also unfair.
